units.tr: Who could believe that the Church of the Lord, which the sun never saw more holy and the earth never bore, which the Holy Spirit of the Lord Jesus Christ himself brought forth from heaven through the preaching of the Word, first through the Apostles and then spread so far and wide through the same men, and which he cherished and defended so long and so wonderfully against constant storms at home and abroad, so that "mercy and truth met together, righteousness and peace kissed each other," who, I say, could believe that from that milk of the Gospel, that upbringing by the Spirit, that worship of incomparable charity and simplicity, it slipped so gradually into human weakness that, by not paying enough attention to the pure use of faith in most places, it at last broke out in nearly all places into a superstitious and plainly idolatrous form of worship of God, into a profane corruption of the articles of faith itself, and into so proud a usurping of absolute lordship that it became careless of both God's right and his judgment, as these last days bear witness? And yet could the name of Church be claimed for it by any faith, while those customs, those rites and those impostures remain in place? "I sit as a queen," it says, "and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow." So let all glory here yield to the one Lord, and not be taken from him, who by his just judgment "has made us err from his ways and hardened our heart so that we did not fear him," as the Church speaks through the Prophet in Isaiah 63. So, I say, he has made his people see hard things; he has given us a wine of stupor to drink, yet he has given a banner to those who fear him, to be raised because of the truth, as the Church also acknowledges in Psalm 60. For whatever has happened from that overturning of the Church down to our own age, this at least had to stand and be believed: that Christ the Lord, once lifted up on high, ought to be proclaimed among all peoples, so that the obedience of all God's elect might be fulfilled and all the rest might be rendered the more subject to God's judgment. How much of this work of God has been accomplished so far, how much still remains to be done, and by what reasoning the whole thing has stood and will stand, he alone knows, who alone does great things with us, and whose name is holy. For although the sincere administration of the Church has long since ceased, and faith has not only been endangered as to its sense and true use, but even the very name of Christianity, as far as men are concerned, has shown a certain force of outward profession rather than either the light of knowledge or integrity of life, yet still, even under that thoroughly step-motherly government of the Church, those marks of God's covenant did not wholly fail, and some reading or rather sprinkling of the Word of God was able to sustain the wretched souls of the godly, which sighed within them, so that their groans and desires were never hidden from the Lord. For "the sanctuary of the Church is the forgiveness of sins," as Augustine writes elegantly. And since the Lord, having taken pity on us, has restored the full light of his Word to his Church, so that one can behold Christ himself as face to face, if one turns the heart earnestly to his Word, as sincerely and clearly as it now shines forth, who will be able to conceive this incomparable benefit of his even in mind, let alone express it in words, and much less acknowledge it in deed! But nevertheless, by his singular mercy his generosity has not so far been in vain, nor will it be in future, however great the ingratitude of us all. It was only ours to see that, freed from that prison and from the dreadful shadow of death, which we often recognise more than we ought, we do not perish in every direction, and turn out much like the others, or even worse. For what are our manners, that we might make progress before God in obedience to his truth, and in ourselves for a serious mortification, to turn back from common luxury and the desires of the flesh, and to gain our neighbours, whoever they are, for the Lord and deserve well of them? When then will that oracle of the Lord to his people stand, "Say to your brothers, 'You are my people,' and to your sisters, 'You have obtained mercy.' Plead with your mother, for she is not my wife and I am not her husband, that she may put away her harlotries from her face and her adulteries from between her breasts" (Hos. 2.)? We hear this in the Church at times, but we are little moved, because we turn our minds elsewhere. Hence that struggle of the Church continues: "a day of distress, a day of rebuke, a day of blasphemy is this day; the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth" (Isa. 37.). May the Lord look upon our desolations and uphold the hope of his people with that arm of his; may he gather his elect from every side, and have mercy on us all, so that at last we may be counted one body and one flesh in Christ the Lord, since his name has been called upon over us. For all extremes press harder and harder, and Satan is wholly intent on bringing the name of the Church into conflict with the truth, and wars rage within and without, and scandals overflow. And we, who rightly condemn blindness in others, do not perceive in ourselves a much more unworthy opening of the eyes, while most of us live for ourselves and seek only our own things, not those of Jesus Christ.

units.tr: An age clever and stubborn in retaining, increasing and spreading the heresies of the previous century. units.la: SEXTA ANNORVM CENTVRIA à VI. imperij Iustiniani primi, finit ad annum XXIII. Heraclij imperatoris, quo ipso anno terraemotus in Palaestina factus est, signum gladij in caelo visum, quod triginta diebus versus Meridiem stetit, & futuram Saracenorum potentiam portendebat.
units.tr: The SIXTH CENTURY of the years, from the 6th year of Justinian the First, ends in the 23rd year of the emperor Heraclius, in which year an earthquake occurred in Palestine, and a sign of a sword was seen in the sky, which stood for thirty days toward the south and portended the future power of the Saracens.

units.la: Ætas ferax, & mater vniuersi, quod postea in orbem terrarum vniuersum ex superioribus haeresibus sparsum est, venenis, & vniuersalis apostasiae, tum in Oriente, tum in Occidente. In hac enim annorum centuria & Papismus & Mahumetismus ortus est. Agnoetae sub Mauricio imperatore, & Gregorio Magno, anno | 572 Tritheita sub Phoca imperatore, & Bonifacio tertio R.E. anno | 574
units.tr: This fruitful age, the mother of all, in which the heresies of earlier times were scattered through the whole world, with their poisons and universal apostasy, both in the East and in the West. For in this century both Papism and Mahumetism arose. The Agnoetae under the emperor Mauricius and Gregory the Great, in the year 572. The Tritheites under the emperor Phocas and Boniface the Third, Bishop of Rome, in the year 574.

units.la: INDEX TERTIUS, UBI ostenditur, in quo doctrina Christianae capite a superioribus haeresibus sit erratum. Omnis autem doctrina Christiana breviter ad haec quatuor capita revocatur, nimirum Decalogum Legis, Symbolum fidei, Orationem Dominicam, & Sacramenta. Ac primum qui in Decalogo Legis errarunt.
units.tr: INDEX THE THIRD, SHOWING in which article of Christian doctrine each of the earlier heresies has erred. All Christian doctrine is briefly reduced to these four heads, namely the Decalogue of the Law, the Creed of faith, the Lord's Prayer, and the Sacraments. And first, those who have erred concerning the Decalogue of the Law.

units.la: DE VERBO DEI scripto.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE WRITTEN WORD OF GOD.

units.la: Verbum Dei scriptum in universum nullam certitudinem habere, sed quemque haereticum recte sentire dicunt Rhetoriani, Lampe-tiani.
units.tr: The Rhetorians and the Lampetians say that the written Word of God has no certainty at all, and that each heretic judges rightly.

units.la: Verbum Dei allegoriis prorsus pervertunt Origenista, Nepotiani, Priscilliani.
units.tr: The Origenists, the Nepotianists and the Priscillianists wholly pervert the Word of God by allegories.

units.la: Revelationes, enthusiasmos & deliria sua pro Dei verbo subiiciunt, & sequuntur Montanista, Pepuziani, Donatista, Enthusiasta, Monachi, Anabaptista.
units.tr: The Montanists, Pepuzians, Donatists, Enthusiasts, Monks and Anabaptists set their own revelations, enthusiasms and ravings in place of the Word of God, and follow them.

units.la: Traditiones humanas praeferunt Dei verbo Bonosiani.
units.tr: The Bonosians prefer human traditions to the Word of God.

units.la: Traditiones humanas Dei verbo aequant authoritate, & quoad constringendas hominum conscientias, Encratita, Manichaei, Papista. Traditiones humanas visionibus, & falsis miraculis commendant Nazareni, Papistae.
units.tr: The Encratites, Manichaeans and Papists put human traditions on a level with the Word of God in authority, and as regards binding men's consciences. The Nazarenes and the Papists commend human traditions by visions and false miracles.

units.la: DE VETERI Testamento.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE OLD TESTAMENT.

units.la: Vetus Testamentum omnino reiiciunt Simo-niani, Caiani, Archontici, Cerdoniani, Marcionita, Apellita, Seueriani, Tatiani, Manichaei.
units.tr: The Simonians, Cainites, Archontics, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Apellites, Severians, Tatianists and Manichaeans reject the Old Testament altogether.

units.la: Veteris Testamenti lectionem in Ecclesia Christiana & sub Euangelio inutilem dicunt Manichaei, Aduersarij Legis & Prophetarum.
units.tr: The Manichaeans, the adversaries of the Law and the Prophets say that reading the Old Testament is useless in the Christian Church and under the Gospel.

units.la: Prophetas veteres a diabolo fuisse conten-dunt Saturniani, Basilidiani.
units.tr: The Saturnians and Basilidians contend that the ancient prophets were from the devil.

units.la: Prophetas abreptitios homines & insanos fuisse dicunt Gnostici, Priscillianistae.
units.tr: The Gnostics and Priscillianists say that the prophets were men carried away and mad.

units.la: Nouos & suos veteribus Prophetis præfe-runt Archontici, Cerdoniani, Marcionitæ, Apel-litæ.
units.tr: The Archontics, Cerdonians, Marcionites and Apellites prefer their own new prophets to the ancient prophets.

units.la: Veteris Testamenti partem tantum a Deo esse dicunt Ptolemaei.
units.tr: The Ptolemaists say that only part of the Old Testament is from God.

units.la: Mosem se esse dixit Noetus.
units.tr: Noetus said that he himself was Moses.

units.la: DE DECALOGO Legis.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE DECALOGUE OF THE LAW.

units.la: Decalogum Legis non Dei, sed infaustæ, cu-iusdam naturæ præceptionem esse aiunt Simoniani, Carpocratiani, & Manichaei.
units.tr: The Simonians, Carpocratians and Manichaeans say that the Decalogue is a precept not of God but of some unlucky nature.

units.la: Promissiones in Lege Dei comprehensas, terrenas tantum esse dicunt Basilidiani, Pepu-siani, Adamitæ, Nepotiani, Serutani.
units.tr: The Basilidians, Pepuzians, Adamites, Nepotianists and Serutians say that the promises contained in the Law of God are merely earthly.

units.la: DE PRIMO DECALOGI præcepto, Non habebis deos, &c.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE FIRST PRECEPT OF THE DECALOGUE, Thou shalt have no other gods, etc.

units.la: Plures deos constituunt, quatuor Tetrathe-tæ, Theodosiani, Angelitæ.
units.tr: The Tetrathetes, Theodosians and Angelites set up several gods, four.

units.la: Tres deos Tritheitæ.
units.tr: The Tritheites set up three gods.

units.la: Duos deos, & duo rerum principia sibi mutuo contraria, alterum bonum, alterum malum, Gnostici, Marcitæ, Cerdoniani, Marcionitæ, Ma-nichæi.
units.tr: The Gnostics, Marcites, Cerdonians, Marcionites and Manichaeans posit two gods and two principles of things, mutually opposed, one good and one evil.

units.la: Alium Iudæorū, alium Christianorum Deum faciunt, eosque sibi contrarios, Saturniniani, Basilidiani, Cerdoniani.
units.tr: The Saturninians, Basilidians and Cerdonians make one God the God of the Jews and another the God of the Christians, and set them against each other.

units.la: Verum Deum etiam Iudæis ipsis ante Christi adventum ignotum fuisse dicunt Menandriani, Saturniniani, Basilidiani, Cerdoniani.
units.tr: The Menandrians, Saturninians, Basilidians and Cerdonians say that the true God was unknown even to the Jews themselves before the coming of Christ.

units.la: Verum Deum falsis attributis, & barbaris nominibus designant Nicolaitæ, Carpocratiani, Valentiniani.
units.tr: The Nicolaitans, Carpocratians and Valentinians describe the true God by false attributes and barbarous names.

units.la: Vegum Deum qualis quantusque est, com-prehendi posse dicunt Aetiani. [?]
units.tr: The Aetians say that the true God, as to what he is and how great he is, can be comprehended. [?]

units.la: Dei essentiam corporeā esse contendunt Manichæi, Tertullianistæ, Audiani, Anthropomor-phitæ, Metangismonitæ.
units.tr: The Manichaeans, Tertullianists, Audians, Anthropomorphites and Metangismonites contend that the essence of God is corporeal.

units.la: Oculis etiam corporeis cerni posse dicunt Euchitæ.
units.tr: The Euchites also say that God can be seen with bodily eyes.

units.la: Verum Deum esse Bython & abyssum illam, de qua Genef.1. Valentiniani. Simonem Magum fuisse verum illum Deum aiunt Simoniani.
units.tr: The Valentinians say that the true God is Bython and that abyss of which Genesis 1 speaks. The Simonians say that Simon Magus was that true God.

units.la: Dæmones familiares pro vero Deo colunt Carpocratiani, Marcita, Seueriani.
units.tr: The Carpocratians, Marcites and Severians worship familiar demons as the true God.

units.la: Magicas artes exercent & probant, tanquam diaboli liberum sit in res omnes imperium; Simoniani, Carpocratiani, Marcita, Seueriani, Helcesaitae, Manichæi, Menandriani.
units.tr: The Simonians, Carpocratians, Marcites, Severians, Helcesaites, Manichaeans and Menandrians practise and approve magic arts, as if the devil had free rule over all things.

units.la: Astra, sydera, & planetas, hominum actiones & vitam moderari aiunt Colarbasii, Priscillianistae.
units.tr: The Colarbasians and Priscillianists say that the stars, the constellations and the planets govern human actions and life.

units.la: Fato vitæ nostræ imperium tanquam Deo tribuunt Bardesanistae, Priscillianistae.
units.tr: The Bardesanists and Priscillianists attribute the rule of our life to fate, as to a god.

units.la: Item certis quibusdam characteribus Valentiniani.
units.tr: Likewise the Valentinians (attribute it) to certain characters.

units.la: Habebis.
units.tr: Thou shalt have.

units.la: Est autem Habere, inuocare, & ore & corde confiteri, in quo peccant sequentes hæreses.
units.tr: To "have" (habere) means to invoke and to confess God with mouth and heart. In this the following heresies go wrong.

units.la: Deum inuocandum docent peregrinis & magicis incantationibus Heracleonitae.
units.tr: The Heracleonites teach that God is to be invoked with foreign and magical incantations.

units.la: Deum confiteri aut negare, dicunt esse rem indifferentem Helcesaitae.
units.tr: The Helcesaites say that confessing or denying God is a matter of indifference.

units.la: Duplicem Dei confessionem faciunt, æqualem inter se, eam quæ solo corde fit, & eam quæ ore, ut euitent persequutiones, Heracleo-nitae.
units.tr: The Heracleonites make a double confession of God, equal to each other: the one made in the heart alone, and the one made with the mouth, so that they may avoid persecutions.

units.la: Negare Deum, & fide Christi, homini Christiano licere docent Macedoniani, Messaliani, Priscillianistae.
units.tr: The Macedonians, Messalians and Priscillianists teach that it is lawful for a Christian man to deny God and the faith of Christ.

units.la: Martyria pro Dei nomine toleranda negant Basilidiani, Gnostici.
units.tr: The Basilidians and Gnostics deny that martyrdom is to be endured for the name of God.

units.la: DE SECUNDO PRÆ-cepto, Non facies tibi sculptile, &c.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE SECOND PRECEPT, Thou shalt not make to thyself a graven image, etc.

units.la: Idola etiam ethnicorum, veluti Jovis, & Mercurij, palàm coli posse docent Simoniani, Basili-diani, Manichæi.
units.tr: The Simonians, Basilidians and Manichaeans teach that the idols of the heathen, such as Jupiter and Mercury, may be worshipped openly.

units.la: Clàm & occultè id fieri debere contendunt Gnostici.
units.tr: The Gnostics contend that this must be done secretly and covertly.

units.la: Idolothyta, & iis vesci, rem esse ἀδιάφορον[?] dicunt Nicolaitæ, Basilidiani, Valentiniani.
units.tr: The Nicolaitans, Basilidians and Valentinians say that eating idol-offerings and partaking of them is a thing indifferent [ἀδιάφορον].

units.la: Angelos colunt Simoniani, Caiani, Angelici.
units.tr: The Simonians, Cainites and Angelics worship angels.

units.la: Imaginem Christi colunt Gnostici, Montani-sta, Helcesaitæ.
units.tr: The Gnostics, Montanists and Helcesaites worship the image of Christ.

units.la: Crucem Christi colunt Armenij.
units.tr: The Armenians worship the cross of Christ.

units.la: Mariam virginem, Collyridiani.
units.tr: The Collyridians (worship) the Virgin Mary.

units.la: Serpentem, Ophitæ.
units.tr: The Ophites (worship) the serpent.

units.la: Satanam, Messaliani, Satanici.
units.tr: The Messalians and Satanians (worship) Satan.

units.la: Cainum, Cainitæ.
units.tr: The Cainites (worship) Cain.

units.la: Sethum, Sethiani.
units.tr: The Sethians (worship) Seth.

units.la: Abelem, Abelonitæ.
units.tr: The Abelonites (worship) Abel.

units.la: Solem, & lunam, & planetas, Manichæi;
units.tr: The Manichaeans (worship) the sun, the moon and the planets;

units.la: Aquam, Helcesaitæ.
units.tr: The Helcesaites (worship) water.

units.la: Heliotropium, & herbas quæ ad solem con-vertuntur, Heliotropitæ.
units.tr: The Heliotropites (worship) the heliotrope and the herbs that turn towards the sun.

units.la: Imagines sanctorum, Papistæ.
units.tr: The Papists (worship) images of the saints.

units.la: DE TERTIO PRÆCE-pto, Non sumes nomen Dei in vanum, &c.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE THIRD PRECEPT, Thou shalt not take the name of God in vain, etc.

units.la: Jurare docent, quasi rem indifferentem, & Manichæi. Mentiri & peierare religionis gratia, licere aiunt Priscillianistae, & Audiani.
units.tr: The Manichaeans teach that swearing is a thing indifferent. The Priscillianists and Audians say that it is lawful to lie and to forswear oneself for the sake of religion.

units.la: Per creaturas iurari posse, docent Manichai.
units.tr: The Manichaeans teach that one may swear by creatures.

units.la: DE QVARTO PRÆCEPTO, Memento diei sabbati, &c.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE FOURTH PRECEPT, Remember the sabbath day, etc.

units.la: Sabbatorum obseruationem hodie necessariam putant Ebionitae, Cerinthiani, Apollinaristae.
units.tr: The Ebionites, Cerinthians and Apollinarists think that the observance of the sabbaths is still necessary today.

units.la: Mosaicas ceremonias in vsum, tanquam necessarias, reuocant Ebionitae, Cerinthiani, Nazareni, Floriniani.
units.tr: The Ebionites, Cerinthians, Nazarenes and Florinians revive the Mosaic ceremonies for use, as necessary.

units.la: Sacrificia Legis retinent, adeo vt oues & boues mactent, Samosateniani, Symmachiani, Armenij, Iacobitae.
units.tr: The Samosatenians, Symmachians, Armenians and Jacobites keep the sacrifices of the Law, so that they slaughter sheep and oxen.

units.la: Ceremonias Legis etiam post mortem & resurrectionem vsum habituras dicunt Apollinaristae.
units.tr: The Apollinarists say that the ceremonies of the Law will be in use even after death and resurrection.

units.la: Deum nouis ceremoniis, & ex Paganorum ritu repetitis, colunt Papistae.
units.tr: The Papists worship God with new ceremonies, revived from the rite of the pagans.

units.la: Deum corporeis exercitationibus colunt, tanquam in iis verus Dei cultus sit positus, Monachi.
units.tr: The Monks worship God with bodily exercises, as if true worship of God were placed in them.

units.la: Deum nouo abstinentiarum genere colunt, tanquam in iis vera sanctitas sita sit, ac quidem carne & animatis abstinent Saturniani, Ebionitae, Taciani, Manichaei, Priscillianistae, Patriciani.
units.tr: The Saturnians, Ebionites, Tatianists, Manichaeans, Priscillianists and Patricians worship God with a new kind of abstinence, as if true holiness lay in it; and indeed they abstain from flesh and from animal foods.

units.la: Vino abstinent Seueriani, Encratitae.
units.tr: The Severians and Encratites abstain from wine.

units.la: Abstinentiam prorsus damnant, quasi rem homini Christiano prorsus inutilem & super-stitiosam Aëriani.
units.tr: The Aerians condemn abstinence altogether, as something wholly useless and superstitious for a Christian man.

units.la: Abstinentiam tanquam cardinem sanctitatis commendant Encratitæ.
units.tr: The Encratites commend abstinence as the hinge of holiness.

units.la: DE QVINTO PRÆCEPTO, Honora patrem, & matrem, &c.
units.tr: ON THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT, Honour thy father and mother, etc.

units.la: Magistratum damnant & tollunt Manichæi, Anabaptistæ.
units.tr: The Manichaeans and the Anabaptists condemn and abolish the magistracy.

units.la: Magistratus authoritatem ad negotia reli-gionis interponendam prorsus negant Donatistæ.
units.tr: The Donatists altogether deny that the authority of the magistrate is to be exercised in matters of religion.

units.la: Iudicia capitalia à Christiano homine exer-ceri posse negant Tertullianistæ.
units.tr: The Tertullianists deny that a Christian man may exercise capital jurisdiction.

units.la: DE SEXTO PRÆCEPTO, Non occides.
units.tr: ON THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT, Thou shalt not kill.

units.la: Hominum societatem fugiunt, tanquam rem homini Christiano illicitam, Feri.
units.tr: The Feri shun fellowship with men, as something unlawful for a Christian.

units.la: Seipsos occidere putant licere hominibus Patriciani, Circumcelliones.
units.tr: The Patricians and the Circumcellions think it lawful for men to kill themselves.

units.la: Homines castrant & mutilant, idque facien-dum docent ad regnum cælorum adpiscendum Valesii.
units.tr: The Valesians castrate and maim men, and teach that this must be done in order to obtain the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Bella omnino damnant, atque vsum gladij, Marcionitæ, Anabaptistæ, Tertullianistæ.
units.tr: The Marcionites, the Anabaptists and the Tertullianists utterly condemn war, and the use of the sword.

units.la: Hæreticos à Magistratu puniendos negant Donatistæ.
units.tr: The Donatists deny that heretics are to be punished by the magistrate.

units.la: DE SEPTIMO PRÆCEPTO, Non mœchaberis.
units.tr: ON THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT, You shall not commit adultery.

units.la: Vxores communes & promiscuas esse debere docent Simoniani, Nicolaitæ, Carpocratiani.
units.tr: The Simonians, Nicolaitans and Carpocratians teach that wives ought to be held in common and promiscuously.

units.la: Incestus admittunt & probant Cataphryges.
units.tr: The Cataphrygians admit and approve incest.

units.la: Pudorem omnem more Cynicorum, & verecundiam tollunt Adamitæ, Feri.
units.tr: The Adamites and the Ferians, after the manner of the Cynics, remove all modesty and shame.

units.la: Damnant matrimonia velut doctrinam diaboli Saturniniani, Taciani, Encratitæ, Adamitæ, Valesii, Apostolici, Origeniani, Manichæi, Hierachitæ.
units.tr: The Saturnilians, Tatianists, Encratites, Adamites, Valesians, Apostolics, Origenians, Manichaeans and Hierachites condemn marriage as a doctrine of the devil.

units.la: Coniugia, vti fidei Christianæ repugnantia, damnant Marciomitæ, Luciani, Priscillianistæ.
units.tr: The Marcionites, Lucianists and Priscillianists condemn marriages as contrary to the Christian faith.

units.la: Coniugia concedunt, vsum tamen coniugij damnant Abelonitæ.
units.tr: The Abelonites concede marriages but condemn the use of marriage.

units.la: Coniugia bene concordantia, etiam inter diuites coniuges dissoluunt Montanistæ, Priscillianistæ.
units.tr: The Montanists and Priscillianists dissolve well-agreeing marriages, even among wealthy spouses.

units.la: Primas nuptias concedunt, secundas autem damnant Cataphryges, Nouatiani, Cathari, Tertullianistæ.
units.tr: The Cataphrygians, Novatians, Cathari and Tertullianists allow first marriages but condemn second ones.

units.la: Semen & menstrua mulierum, tanquam res diuinas, excipiunt & lingunt Nicolaitæ, Manichæi.
units.tr: The Nicolaitans and Manichaeans take up the semen and the menstrual fluids of women as if they were holy things, and lick them.

units.la: Semen hominis vt impurum in terram spargunt Origeniani.
units.tr: The Origenians scatter the semen of man on the ground, as something impure.

units.la: DE OCTAVO PRÆCEPTO, Non furaberis.
units.tr: ON THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT, You shall not steal.

units.la: Propria quædam à Christianis possideri posse negant Apostolici, Iesuitæ, Anabaptistæ.
units.tr: The Apostolici, Jesuits, Anabaptists deny that Christians can possess any private property.

units.la: In otio & inertia vitam Christianam constituunt Messaliani, Euchetæ, Monachi.
units.tr: The Messalians, Euchites, monks make the Christian life consist in idleness and inactivity.

units.la: DE NONO PRÆCEPTO, Non falsum testimonium, &c.
units.tr: ON THE NINTH COMMANDMENT, Thou shalt not bear false witness, etc.

units.la: Mentiri homini Christiano licere putant Messaliani, Euchetæ, Priscillianistæ.
units.tr: The Messalians, Euchites and Priscillianists think it lawful for a Christian man to lie.

units.la: DE DECIMO PRÆCEPTO, Non concupiscēs. DE SYMBOLO FIDEI, quod ex Euangelio colligitur.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE TENTH COMMANDMENT, "Thou shalt not covet." CONCERNING THE CREED OF FAITH, as it is gathered from the Gospel.

units.la: Ac primùm, Euangelia plura quàm nostra quatuor habent Nazareni.
units.tr: First, the Nazarenes have more Gospels than our four.

units.la: Euangelia alia pro nostris substituunt Ebio-nitæ, Apostolici.
units.tr: The Ebionites and the Apostolici substitute other Gospels for ours.

units.la: Euangelia quatuor fingunt, quæ diuersis temporibus durarint, scilicet ante diluuium, post diluuium, à Mose, & à Christo, Valentiniani.
units.tr: The Valentinians invent four Gospels which lasted through different periods: namely before the flood, after the flood, from Moses, and from Christ.

units.la: Credo.
units.tr: I believe.

units.la: Fidem nobis esse naturalem, non Dei donum dicunt Basilidiani, Valentiniani, Pelagiani.
units.tr: The Basilidians, Valentinians and Pelagians say that faith is natural to us and not a gift of God.

units.la: Fidei secretum & mysterium paucis manifestandum contendunt Basilidiani, Papistæ.
units.tr: The Basilidians and the Papists maintain that the secret and mystery of faith is to be revealed to few.

units.la: Fidem esse solam & nudam Euangelij cognitionem, quæ bona opera velut fructus adiuncta non habeat, docent Gnostici.
units.tr: The Gnostics teach that faith is only the bare knowledge of the Gospel, which has no good works joined to it as its fruit.

units.la: Opera bona à fide uti rem illi repugnantem, separant Simoniaci, Basilidiani, Libertini.
units.tr: The Simonians, Basilidians and Libertines separate good works from faith, as if the two were incompatible.

units.la: Ab operibus bonis, quæ Lege Dei præscribuntur, liberatos nos esse, eúmque esse fidei Christianæ fructum, dicunt Archontici, Antitactæ, Valesii.
units.tr: The Archontics, Antitactae and Valesians say that we are freed from good works, which are prescribed by the Law of God, and that this is the fruit of Christian faith.

units.la: Opera omnia bona Lege Dei præcepta, ne-gant nobis Christianis sectanda Simoniani, Antitactæ.
units.tr: The Simonians and Antitactae deny that all good works commanded by the Law of God are to be pursued by us Christians.

units.la: Eleemosynas quę pauperibus fiunt, damnant Manichæi, Messaliani.
units.tr: The Manichaeans and Messalians condemn alms given to the poor.

units.la: Turpia facere suadent Origeniani, Messaliani.
units.tr: The Origenians and Messalians urge people to do shameful things.

units.la: Omni turpi libidini inseruiunt, & inseruien-dum docent Carpocratiani, Paterniani, Venustiani, Ethicoprocopta.
units.tr: The Carpocratians, Paterynians, Venustians and Ethicoprocts serve every shameful lust, and teach that it must be served.

units.la: Opera bona & mala, res esse indifferentes natura, sed opinione hominum tantum distin-gui docent Carpocratiani.
units.tr: The Carpocratians teach that good and bad works are by nature indifferent things, distinguished only by the opinion of men.

units.la: Opera futilia & inania pro causis salutis con-stituunt, veluti utrium gestationem, Ascitæ:
units.tr: The Ascites set up futile and empty works as causes of salvation, such as carrying bladders about.

units.la: Silentium, Pattalorinchitæ, Silentiarij.
units.tr: The Pattalorynchites and Silentiarii set up silence.

units.la: Nuditatem, Adamitæ, Nudipedales.
units.tr: The Adamites and Nudipedalians set up nakedness.

units.la: Cibos, & colores vestium, Monachi, Iesuitæ.
units.tr: The Monks and Jesuits set up particular foods and colours of clothing.

units.la: De meritis operum.
units.tr: Concerning the merits of works.

units.la: Fidei fructus maximi sunt duo, Iustificatio, Sanctificatio. Iustificationem meritis operum nostrorum tribuunt Cathari, Hierachitæ, Meletiani, Donatistæ, Pelagiani, [?]Monachi, Anabaptistæ, Iustitiarij, Operistæ, Papistæ.
units.tr: The two greatest fruits of faith are justification and sanctification. The Cathari, Hierakites, Meletians, Donatists, Pelagians, Monks, Anabaptists, Iustitiarii, Operists and Papists ascribe justification to the merits of our works.

units.la: Sanctificationem, siue vitæ & spiritus renouationem, dicunt esse resurrectionem carnis Hymenæus, [?]Menandriani.
units.tr: Hymenaeus and the Menandrians say that sanctification, or the renewal of life and spirit, is the resurrection of the flesh.

units.la: Vitæ sanctitatem irrident Basilidiani, Carpo-cratiani, Nicolaitæ, Valentiniani, Archontici.
units.tr: The Basilidians, Carpocratians, Nicolaitans, Valentinians and Archontics mock the holiness of life.

units.la: Neminem ad sancte viuendum compellendum esse volunt Donatistæ.
units.tr: The Donatists hold that no one ought to be compelled to live holily.

units.la: Exercitia pietatis omnia repudiant Aeriani, Iouinianistæ.
units.tr: The Aerians and Jovinianists reject all exercises of piety.

units.la: In Deum.
units.tr: Concerning God.

units.la: Deum numen quoddam unicum esse & solitarium tanquam mundi monarcham unum dicunt Apellitæ, Messaliani, Deitæ, Monarchitæ.
units.tr: The Apellites, Messalians, Deists and Monarchians say that God is a certain single and solitary divine power, one as the monarch of the world.

units.la: Vnam esse in Trinitate personam, quæ diuersis nominibus, Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti appelletur, dicunt Simoniani, Ptolemæi, Colarba-sii, Montanistæ, Noetiani, Praxeani, Sabelliani, A-pollinaristæ, Priscillianistæ.
units.tr: The Simonians, Ptolemaeans, Colarbasians, Montanists, Noetians, Praxeans, Sabellians, Apollinarians and Priscillianists say that there is one person in the Trinity, who is called by different names: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

units.la: Trinitatem esse extensionem vnius eiusdem-que rei, vti ceræ, docent [?]Marcelliani.
units.tr: The Marcellians teach that the Trinity is one and the same thing extended, like wax.

units.la: Personas in Trinitate esse vti vnius lucernæ duo luminaria, Hierachitæ.
units.tr: The Hierakites teach that the persons in the Trinity are like two lights of one lamp.

units.la: Personas esse vti vasa alia in aliis contenta, & pelles in sese implicatas, [?]Metangismonitæ.
units.tr: The Metangismonites teach that the persons are like vessels contained one within another, and skins folded into one another.

units.la: Tres personas esse tres Deos diuersos & se-paratos, Tritheitæ, Triformiani.
units.tr: The Tritheites and Triformians hold that the three persons are three distinct and separate Gods.

units.la: Personarum quaternitatem constituunt Mar-citæ, Apollinaristæ, Tetratheitæ.
units.tr: The Marcites, Apollinarians and Tetratheites set up a quaternity of persons.

units.la: M.iiij. Tres personas esse tres tantum qualitates, Aetiani.
units.tr: M.iiij. The Aetians hold that the three persons are merely three qualities.

units.la: Omnipotentem.
units.tr: The Almighty.

units.la: Homines esse sub potestate malorum Angelorum, non autem Dei, contendunt Carpocratiani, Messaliani.
units.tr: The Carpocratians and Messalians contend that men are under the power of evil angels, and not under the power of God.

units.la: Deum neque iustum esse, neque huius mundi administratorem, Coluthiani.
units.tr: The Coluthians hold that God is neither just nor the administrator of this world.

units.la: Mundum ab Atlante sustineri & gestari dicunt Manichaei.
units.tr: The Manichaeans say that the world is held up and carried by Atlas.

units.la: Creatorem caeli & terrae.
units.tr: Maker of heaven and earth.

units.la: Mundum hunc esse opus indignum Deo bono dicunt Marcionita.
units.tr: The Marcionites say that this world is a work unworthy of the good God.

units.la: Mundum ab Angelis, non a Deo creatum, asserunt Simoniani, Nicolaita, Menandriani, Archontici.
units.tr: The Simonians, Nicolaitans, Menandrians and Archontics assert that the world was created by angels, not by God.

units.la: Mundum a septem tantum Angelis creatum dicunt Saturniniani, Basilidiani.
units.tr: The Saturnians and Basilidians say that the world was created by seven angels only.

units.la: Mundum ab inferioribus Angelis & diabolo conditum asserunt Cerinthiani, Luciferiani, Carpocratiani. Valentiniani, Manichaei, Priscillianista.
units.tr: The Cerinthians, Luciferians, Carpocratians, Valentinians, Manichaeans and Priscillianists assert that the world was founded by inferior angels and the devil.

units.la: Mundi creatorem esse malum Deum dicunt Cerdoniani, Marcionita, Apellita.
units.tr: The Cerdonians, Marcionites and Apellites say that the creator of the world is an evil God.

units.la: Mundi creatorem non esse Deum Abrahami, sed alium dicunt Caiani.
units.tr: The Caianites say that the creator of the world is not the God of Abraham, but another.

units.la: Mundum a Christo tanquam Patris instrumento conditum dicunt Arriani, Duliani.
units.tr: The Arians and Dulianists say that the world was created by Christ as the instrument of the Father.

units.la: De mundi creatione fabulosa narrant Gnostici, Manichaei.
units.tr: The Gnostics and Manichaeans tell fabulous stories about the creation of the world.

units.la: Omnia haec esse Dei substantiam dicunt Manichaei. Mundos innumerabiles esse, Ophei.
units.tr: The Manichaeans say that all these things are the substance of God. The Opheites hold that there are innumerable worlds.

units.la: Alium mundum esse præter hunc qui sit in-genitus, Perata.
units.tr: The Peratae hold that there is another world besides this one, which is unbegotten.

units.la: Materiam mundi Deo coæternam esse, Se-leuciani, Hermiani, Procliani, Hermogeniani.
units.tr: The Seleucians, Hermians, Proclians and Hermogenians hold that the matter of the world is coeternal with God.

units.la: Ex sudore & metu Æonum factum esse mun-dum, Valentiniani, Secundiani.
units.tr: The Valentinians and Secundians hold that the world was made from the sweat and fear of the Aeons.

units.la: Principia hæc tria esse increata nimirum, a-quam, ignem & tenebras, Audiani.
units.tr: The Audians hold that there are three uncreated principles, namely water, fire and darkness.

units.la: Aquam esse Deo coæternam, Aquei.
units.tr: The Aqueans hold that water is coeternal with God.

units.la: Mundi huius statum esse æternum, Eter-nales.
units.tr: The Eternalists hold that the state of this world is eternal.

units.la: De Angelis.
units.tr: Concerning the angels.

units.la: Angelos esse ex Dei sapientia velut matre, propagatione natos, Basilidiani, Gnostici, Ar-chontici.
units.tr: The Basilidians, Gnostics and Archontics hold that the angels were born by propagation from the wisdom of God as from a mother.

units.la: Ex concupiscentia tenebrarum & impetu in lucem, Nicolaitæ.
units.tr: The Nicolaitans hold that they were born from the lust of darkness and the rush toward the light.

units.la: Angelos barbaris nominibus & magicis ap-pellant Nicolaitæ, Gnostici, Seueriani.
units.tr: The Nicolaitans, Gnostics and Severians call the angels by barbarous and magical names.

units.la: Angelos præfici cælis, quenque suo orbi, Ba-silidiani.
units.tr: The Basilidians hold that angels are set over the heavens, each over his own sphere.

units.la: Bonos Angelos revera cum mulieribus co-ire ad homines procreandos, Sethiani.
units.tr: The Sethians hold that the good angels actually had intercourse with women in order to beget human beings.

units.la: Diabolum esse natum ex tricesimo Æone, Valentiniani, Archontici.
units.tr: The Valentinians and Archontics hold that the devil was born from the thirtieth Aeon.

units.la: Diabolum esse corporeum, Messaliani.
units.tr: The Messalians hold that the devil is corporeal.

units.la: De cælo.
units.tr: Concerning heaven.

units.la: Cælos esse alios ex aliis fluentes, & numero 365. Basilidiani.
units.tr: The Basilidians hold that the heavens flow one from another, and that there are 365 of them.

units.la: Stellas & astra esse prædita ratione, Priscillia[?]nistæ.
units.tr: The Priscillianists hold that the stars and constellations are endowed with reason.

units.la: De homine.
units.tr: Concerning man.

units.la: Adam & Euam non esse a Deo creatos, Ma-nichæi.
units.tr: That Adam and Eve were not created by God: Manichaeans.

units.la: Hominem constare triplici essentia, Hera-cleonitæ.
units.tr: That man consists of a threefold essence: Heracleonites.

units.la: Carnem hominis a Deo non esse, Patriciani,
units.tr: That the flesh of man is not from God: Patricians,

units.la: Partes corporis nostri inferiores Diaboli opus esse, Paterniani, Eunomiani, Ethicoprocoptæ.
units.tr: That the lower parts of our body are the work of the Devil: Paternians, Eunomians, Ethicoprocoptae.

units.la: Mulieres detestantur Archontici, Seueriani.
units.tr: They detest women: Archontics, Severians.

units.la: Humanum femen detestantur Origeniani, Manichæi.
units.tr: They detest human semen: Origenians, Manichaeans.

units.la: Hominis primi nuditatem imitantur Adamitæ.
units.tr: They imitate the nakedness of the first man: Adamites.

units.la: Adamum moriturum fuisse, etsi non peccasset, Pelagiani, Celestiani.
units.tr: That Adam would have died even if he had not sinned: Pelagians, Celestians.

units.la: Hominem creatum ad similitudinem splendoris cuiusdam cœlestis, non ad Dei imaginem, Saturniniani.
units.tr: That man was created in the likeness of a certain heavenly splendour, not in the image of God: Saturninians.

units.la: In homine imaginem Dei esse in corpore, nō in anima, Melitonij, Anthropomorphitæ.
units.tr: That the image of God in man is in the body and not in the soul: Melitonians, Anthropomorphites.

units.la: Animam hominis ab Angelis non a Deo creatam esse, Seleuciani, Hermiani, Procliani.
units.tr: That the soul of man was created by angels and not by God: Seleucians, Hermians, Proclians.

units.la: Animam hominis esse corpoream, & ex carne transfundi, Luciferiani, Tertullianistæ.
units.tr: That the soul of man is corporeal and is transmitted from the flesh: Luciferians, Tertullianists.

units.la: Anima hominis esse mortalem, & cum corpore interire, Arabici.
units.tr: That the soul of man is mortal and perishes with the body: Arabians.

units.la: Animam hominis diuinæ naturæ partem esse & eiusdem cum eo essentiæ: Gnostici, Manichæi, Priscilliani stæ.
units.tr: That the soul of man is a part of the divine nature and of the same essence as it: Gnostics, Manichaeans, Priscillianists.

units.la: Animam hominis & brutorum animantium esse eiusdem essentiæ & naturæ, Nazarei, Ma-nichæi. nichæi.
units.tr: That the soul of man and of the brute animals is of the same essence and nature: Nazarenes, Manichaeans.

units.la: Animam hominis esse duplicis & diuersæ naturæ, quarum vna sit à Deo, altera non, Gnostici, Manichæi.
units.tr: That the soul of man is of a double and diverse nature, of which one part is from God and the other is not: Gnostics, Manichaeans.

units.la: Animas hominum semper fuisse, sed in cælis, Origenistæ.
units.tr: That the souls of men have always existed, but in the heavens: Origenists.

units.la: Animam ex anima nasci, Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: That the soul is born from the soul: Apollinarians.

units.la: Animas hominum in corpora migrare post mortem, Tertullij.
units.tr: That the souls of men migrate into bodies after death: Tertullians.

units.la: Animas hominum sceleratorum post mortem diabolos fieri, Tertullij, Tertullianistæ.
units.tr: That the souls of wicked men become devils after death: Tertullians, Tertullianists.

units.la: Vinum damnant quasi non Dei opus, Seueriani.
units.tr: They condemn wine as if it were not the work of God: Severians.

units.la: De malis & peccatis.
units.tr: Concerning evils and sins.

units.la: Mala & peccata à Deo creata, Valentiniani, [?]Manichæi, Seleuciani, Hermiani, Floriniani.
units.tr: That evils and sins were created by God: Valentinians, [?]Manichaeans, Seleucians, Hermians, Florinians.

units.la: Et in Iesum Christum.
units.tr: And in Jesus Christ.

units.la: Iesum à Christo vt duas personas separant Gnostici, Cerinthiani, Colarbasii.
units.tr: They separate Jesus from Christ as two persons: Gnostics, Cerinthians, Colarbasians.

units.la: In Christo aliam esse diuinitatis, aliam esse humanitatis personam, Nestoriani, Christolytæ.
units.tr: That in Christ there is one person of the divinity and another of the humanity: Nestorians, Christolytes.

units.la: Iesum Christum in tres personas diuidunt Valentiniani.
units.tr: They divide Jesus Christ into three persons: Valentinians.

units.la: Christum tricorporeum ex tribus mundi partibus constituunt Perata.
units.tr: They make Christ tricorporeal, constituted from three parts of the world: Perates.

units.la: Christos duos faciunt Helcesaitæ.
units.tr: They make two Christs: Elkesaites.

units.la: Christum esse dicunt Simonem Magum, Si-moniani:
units.tr: They say that Simon Magus is Christ: Simonians;

units.la: Sethum, Sethiani:
units.tr: Seth: Sethians;

units.la: Serpentem, Ophitæ, [?]Manichæi.
units.tr: A serpent: Ophites, [?]Manichaeans.

units.la: Iesum & seruatore se esse dixit [?]Menander.
units.tr: [?]Menander said that he himself was Jesus and the Saviour.

units.la: Iesum animarum tantum, non etiam corporum nostrorum redemptorem esse dicunt Ma-tthæi[?].
units.tr: They say that Jesus is the redeemer of souls only, and not also of our bodies: Matthaeans[?].

units.la: Iesum superiorum tantum, non etiam inferiorum corporis nostri partium redemptorem esse volunt Paterniani, Postelliani.
units.tr: They wish Jesus to be the redeemer only of the higher parts, and not also of the lower parts of our body: Paternians, Postellians.

units.la: Filium eius unigenitum.
units.tr: His only-begotten Son.

units.la: Christum esse ποίημα[?], id est metem[?], creatam, sed primogenitam contendunt Basilidiani, Orige-nistæ.
units.tr: They contend that Christ is a made thing [ποίημα], that is, a creature, but the firstborn: Basilideans, Origenists.

units.la: Christum non esse Dei creatoris sed alterius filium, Marcianitæ.
units.tr: That Christ is not the Son of the Creator God but of another: Marcionites.

units.la: Christum esse creaturam natura, sed gratia Deum, Origenistæ, Arriani.
units.tr: That Christ is a creature by nature but God by grace: Origenists, Arians.

units.la: Christi Filii Dei ex Dei Patris semine generationem fabulosam narrant Heracleonitæ, Bar-desanistæ[?].
units.tr: They tell a fabulous story of the generation of the Son of God from the seed of God the Father: Heracleonites, Bardesanites[?].

units.la: Christum esse ex Æonibus, non ex Deo, Va-lentiniani, Seleuciani, Colarbasii.
units.tr: That Christ is from the Aeons and not from God: Valentinians, Seleucians, Colarbasians.

units.la: Christum fuisse Filium Dei, sed adoptivum, Bonosiani.
units.tr: That Christ was the Son of God, but by adoption: Bonosians.

units.la: Christum fuisse ab æterno quidem apud Pa-trem, nō tamen ab æterno Filium, vel ab eo genitum, Nativitarii.
units.tr: That Christ indeed existed from eternity with the Father, but was not the Son from eternity, nor begotten by him: Nativitarians.

units.la: Christum ante incarnationem ex Maria virgine omnino non fuisse, sed nec Deum, Ar-temonitæ, Samosateniani, Marcelliani, Photiniani, Luciani.
units.tr: That Christ before the incarnation from the Virgin Mary did not exist at all, nor was he God: Artemonites, Samosatenians, Marcellians, Photinians, Lucianists.

units.la: Patrem ab æterno geniturientem tandem in virgine Maria genuisse Filium suum, Servetiani.
units.tr: That the Father, having conceived from eternity, at length brought forth his Son in the Virgin Mary: Servetians.

units.la: Christum ex non entibus factum, Arriani, Exoucontii.
units.tr: That Christ was made out of non-beings: Arians, Exoucontians.

units.la: Christum non esse αὐτόθεον[?], sed Patre minorem. rem.i.deificatum, Arriani, Donatistæ.
units.tr: That Christ is not autotheos [αὐτόθεος], but less than the Father, that is, a deified being: Arians, Donatists.

units.la: Christum esse virtute & natura inferiorem Melchisedeco, Melchisedeciani.
units.tr: That Christ is inferior in power and nature to Melchizedek: Melchizedekians.

units.la: Christum Patri ὁμοιούσιον tantum, Acatiani, Samiarriani, Macedoniani.
units.tr: That Christ is only homoousios [ὁμοιούσιος], of like essence, with the Father: Acacians, Samosatenians-Arians, Macedonians.

units.la: Patri ὑπερούσιον [?], Eunomiani.
units.tr: That Christ is hyperousios [ὑπερούσιος], above essence, with respect to the Father: Eunomians.

units.la: Patri ἀνόμοιον [?], Anomoei, Aetiani.
units.tr: That Christ is anomoios [ἀνόμοιος], unlike, with respect to the Father: Anomoeans, Aetians.

units.la: Patris seruum, Duliani.
units.tr: That Christ is the servant of the Father: Dulianists.

units.la: Diuinam Christi naturam quædam ignorafse, Agnoetæ.
units.tr: That some were ignorant of the divine nature of Christ: Agnoetae.

units.la: Diuinam naturam in Christo fuisse tantum post incarnationem, Monophysitæ.
units.tr: That the divine nature was in Christ only after the incarnation: Monophysites.

units.la: Dominum nostrum.
units.tr: Our Lord.

units.la: Caput Ecclesiæ præter Christum, Papam constituunt Papistæ.
units.tr: They set up the Pope as head of the Church besides Christ: Papists.

units.la: Christi multa facta improbant Theocatagnostæ.
units.tr: They disapprove of many of Christ's deeds: Theocatagnostae.

units.la: Conceptum ex Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: Conceived by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Christum conceptum ex concubitu ad morem caeterorum hominum afferunt Carpocratiani:
units.tr: They assert that Christ was conceived from intercourse, as with other men: Carpocratians;

units.la: Ex Iosephi & Mariæ coitu, Ebionitæ, Cerinthiani, Theodotiani.
units.tr: From the intercourse of Joseph and Mary: Ebionites, Cerinthians, Theodotians.

units.la: Natum ex Maria virgine.
units.tr: Born of the Virgin Mary.

units.la: Christum in carne venisse & hominem factum negant Simoniani, Christolytæ, Proclitæ.
units.tr: They deny that Christ came in the flesh and was made man: Simonians, Christolytes, Proclites.

units.la: Christum duntaxat fuisse hominem, sed propter maiores progressus virtutum perfectiorem caeteris, Ebionitæ, Cerinthiani, Artemonitæ, Alogi, Theodotiani, Melchisedeciani, Manichæi.
units.tr: That Christ was only a man, but more perfect than others because of his greater progress in virtues: Ebionites, Cerinthians, Artemonites, Alogi, Theodotians, Melchizedekians, Manichaeans.

units.la: De unione naturarum.
units.tr: On the union of the natures.

units.la: Naturam humanam in Christo a divina suis-se absorptam, Eutychiani, Iacobitæ, Armenij.
units.tr: That the human nature in Christ was absorbed by the divine: the Eutychians, Jacobites, Armenians.

units.la: Naturam humanam deificatam, i. mutatam in divinam & illi adæquatam fuisse, Nestoriani, Servetani, Ubiquitarij.
units.tr: That the human nature was deified, that is, changed into the divine and made equal to it: the Nestorians, Servetians, Ubiquitarians.

units.la: Ex duabus naturis unum quiddam mixtū & tertium factum esse in Christo, Timotheani.
units.tr: That one mixed thing, a third made out of the two natures, exists in Christ: the Timotheans.

units.la: Quod tertium, alij dicunt mortale fuisse, ne-pe Theodotiani: alij immortale, nempe, Caiani.
units.tr: Some say this third thing was mortal, namely the Theodotians; others that it was immortal, namely the Caianites.

units.la: Filium Dei in filiū Mariæ descendisse in Baptismo, ɔ[?]Manichæi.
units.tr: That the Son of God descended into the son of Mary at baptism: and the Manichaeans.

units.la: Verbum ipsum Dei in carnem esse mutatum, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: That the Word of God itself was changed into flesh: and the Apollinarians.

units.la: Divinam naturam in Christo passam esse, Theopaschitæ.
units.tr: That the divine nature in Christ suffered: the Theopaschites.

units.la: Divinam naturam & humanam manere quidē in Christo, sed earum proprietates esse confusas, ɔ[?]Acephali, Severitæ.
units.tr: That the divine and human natures do indeed remain in Christ, but their properties are confused: and the Acephali and Severians.

units.la: Christum, quatenus homo, non habere propriam voluntatem, quia confusa fit humana natura & versa in divinam, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: That Christ, as man, does not have a proper will, because the human nature is confused and turned into the divine: and the Apollinarians.

units.la: Unam tantūm in Christo voluntatem fuisse, Monothelitæ.
units.tr: That there was only one will in Christ: the Monothelites.

units.la: Ex Maria.
units.tr: From Mary.

units.la: Christum negant ex Maria assumpsisse corpus, Valentiniani, Secundiani, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: They deny that Christ assumed a body from Mary: the Valentinians, Secundians, and the Apollinarians.

units.la: Christum ex Davidis semine esse negant Tatiani, ɔ[?]Manichæi.
units.tr: They deny that Christ was of the seed of David: the Tatians, and the Manichaeans.

units.la: Christum ex Maria virgine natum negant hominem verum fuisse, & passum, quia caro hu-mana mana sit res polluta, Ophitæ, Cerdoniani, Marcionitæ, Apellitæ, & Manichæi, Autartòdochitæ.
units.tr: Those who deny that Christ, born of the virgin Mary, was a true man and suffered, because human flesh is a polluted thing: the Ophites, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Apellites, and Manichaeans, Autartodocetae.

units.la: Christi corpus ex quatuor elementis & fide-ribus fuisse compositum dicunt Apellitæ.
units.tr: The Apellites say that the body of Christ was composed of four elements and phantoms.

units.la: Corpus ex Maria assumptū fuisse ab ipsa conceptione impasibile dicunt Armenij.
units.tr: The Armenians say that the body assumed from Mary was impassible from the very moment of conception.

units.la: Christū corpus cæleste & spirituale, non autem terrenum aut humanum, habuisse volunt Valentiniani, Marcionitæ, Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: They wish Christ to have had a heavenly and spiritual body, not an earthly or human one: the Valentinians, Marcionites, Apollinarians.

units.la: Christum animam humanam negant assumpsisse, sed tantum corpus, Arriani, Eunomiani.
units.tr: They deny that Christ assumed a human soul, but only a body: the Arians, Eunomians.

units.la: Christum animam quidem assumpsisse cum corpore, sed tantum vegetatiuam, nō etiam rationalem, Apollinaristæ.
units.tr: That Christ assumed a soul along with the body, but only a vegetative soul and not also a rational one: the Apollinarians.

units.la: Mariam virginem mansisse negant, Antidico-marianitæ, Heluidiani.
units.tr: They deny that the virgin Mary remained a virgin: the Antidicomarianites, Helvidians.

units.la: Passum sub Pontio Pilato.
units.tr: Suffered under Pontius Pilate.

units.la: Fictè & putatiuè tantùm, non autem verè passum Christū dicunt Simoniani, Saturniniani, Basilidiani, Marcitæ, Cerdoniani, Marcionitæ, Apellitæ, Docetæ, Manichæi.
units.tr: They say that Christ suffered only feignedly and in appearance, not truly: the Simonians, Saturnians, Basilidians, Marcites, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Apellites, Docetae, Manichaeans.

units.la: Christi diuinitatem passam esse, Theopaschi-tæ, Autartodocetæ, Eutychiani, Seueritæ, Armenij.
units.tr: That the divinity of Christ suffered: the Theopaschites, Autartodocetae, Eutychians, Severians, Armenians.

units.la: Patrem passum esse, quia eadem sit cum Filio persona, Noetiani, Sabelliani, qui & Patripassia-ni dicuntur.
units.tr: That the Father suffered, because he is the same person as the Son: the Noetians, Sabellians, who are also called Patripassians.

units.la: Crucifixum & mortuum.
units.tr: Was crucified and died.

units.la: Mortem negant esse peccati poenam, Pela-giani, Cœlestiani.
units.tr: They deny that death is the punishment of sin: the Pelagians, Celestians.

units.la: Sepultum.
units.tr: Was buried.

units.la: Qui descendit ad inferos.
units.tr: Descended into hell.

units.la: Christum descensu suo liberasse ab inferis animas reproborum dicunt Marcionitæ, Liberatores.
units.tr: They say that by his descent Christ freed from hell the souls of the reprobate: the Marcionites, the Liberatores.

units.la: Resurrexit a mortuis.
units.tr: Rose from the dead.

units.la: Christum resurrexisse negant Cerinthiani.
units.tr: They deny that Christ rose again: the Cerinthians.

units.la: Post resurrectionem Christum veras vulne-rum cicatrices in corpore habuisse negant Ma-nichæi.
units.tr: They deny that after the resurrection Christ had true scars of his wounds in his body: the Manichaeans.

units.la: Christum post resurrectionem hic fuisse per octodecim menses dicunt Gnostici.
units.tr: They say that Christ remained here after the resurrection for eighteen months: the Gnostics.

units.la: Ascendit in cælum.
units.tr: Ascended into heaven.

units.la: Christi in cælum ascensionem esse corporis illius in quatuor elementa dissolutionem dicut Apellitæ.
units.tr: They say that the ascension of Christ was the dissolution of that body into the four elements: the Apellites.

units.la: Christi corpus astris & sideribus alligatum esse, & maximè globo solis affixum, Manichæi, Seleuciani, Hermiani.
units.tr: That the body of Christ is bound to the stars and constellations, and especially fixed to the orb of the sun: the Manichaeans, Seleucians, Hermians.

units.la: Christi ascensionem esse ex his terris dispa-ritionem & euanescentiam tantùm, Vbiquitarij.
units.tr: That the ascension of Christ was only a disappearance and vanishing from this earth: the Ubiquitarians.

units.la: Christi animam tantum in cælum ascendisse, non etiam corpus, Carpocratiani.
units.tr: That only the soul of Christ ascended into heaven, not the body: the Carpocratians.

units.la: Christi Deitatem duntaxat in cælum ascendisse, Christolytæ.
units.tr: That only the deity of Christ ascended into heaven: the Christolytae.

units.la: Sedet ad dexteram, &c.
units.tr: Sits at the right hand, etc.

units.la: Christum non sedere in carne ad dexteram Patris, Seleuciani, Hermiani, Proclianitæ.
units.tr: That Christ does not sit in the flesh at the right hand of the Father: the Seleucians, Hermians, Proclianites.

units.la: Venturus ut iudicet vivos & mortuos. Credo in Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum esse tantum nomen energiæ & virtutis,non autem essentię, dicunt Simo-niani.
units.tr: They say that the Holy Spirit is only a name of energy and power, and not of essence: the Simonians.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum esse Melchisedech, Hie-rachitæ.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is Melchizedek: the Hierachites.

units.la: Spiritum sanctū esse sororem Christi, Hel-cesaitæ [?].
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is the sister of Christ: the Helcesaites [?].

units.la: Spiritum sanctum se esse dixit Manes siue Manichæus.
units.tr: Manes, or Manichaeus, said that he himself was the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum se & suum scortum appel-lauit Simon Magus, Montanus.
units.tr: Simon Magus and Montanus called the Holy Spirit themselves and their own harlot.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum esse creaturam, non autem Deum, Origenistæ, Arriani, Acatiani, Macedo-niani, Aetiani, Feri.
units.tr: That the Holy Spirit is a creature and not God: the Origenists, Arians, Acacians, Macedonians, Aetians, Feri.

units.la: Spiritus sancti partes & essentiam, ipsam per omnes creaturas esse diffusam; Macedoniani, Seruetani.
units.tr: That the parts and essence of the Holy Spirit are diffused through all creatures: the Macedonians, Servetians.

units.la: Spiritum sanctum negant esse datum Apostolis quantum satis est, Cataphryges; Montanistæ, Manichæi.
units.tr: They deny that the Holy Spirit was given to the Apostles in sufficient measure: the Cataphrygians, Montanists, Manichaeans.

units.la: Credo Ecclesiam sanctam. De prædestinatione quæ fundamen-tum est Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: I believe the holy Church. On predestination, which is the foundation of the Church.

units.la: Prædestinationem ullam esse negant Pelagia-ni, Celestiani.
units.tr: They deny that there is any predestination: the Pelagians, Celestians.

units.la: Prædestinationem & electionē non Dei gratiæ, sed nostris operibus tribuunt Basilidiani, Caiani, Pelagiani, Papistæ.
units.tr: They ascribe predestination and election not to the grace of God but to our works: the Basilidians, Caianites, Pelagians, Papists.

units.la: Prædestinationē astris & fato tribuunt Bar-desanistæ, Priscillianistæ.
units.tr: They ascribe predestination to the stars and to fate: the Bardesanists, Priscillianists.

units.la: Prædestinatione ad sceleta quælibet perpe-tranda abutuntur Prædestinati dicti, Libertini.
units.tr: They abuse predestination to justify committing any wickedness whatever: the so-called Predestinarians, Libertines.

units.la: Reprobatos laudant & colunt tanquam Dei instrumenta praestantissima, Caiani, Marcioni-ta, Cerinthiani, Pepuziani.
units.tr: They praise and worship the reprobate as the most excellent instruments of God: the Caianites, Marcionites, Cerinthians, Pepuzians.

units.la: Adamum reprobatum affirmant Tatiani.
units.tr: The Tatians affirm that Adam was reprobate.

units.la: Ecclesiam.
units.tr: The Church.

units.la: Ecclesiam certis locis assignant. Pepuziani, Papistae.
units.tr: They assign the Church to certain places: the Pepuzians, Papists.

units.la: Ecclesiam propter Episcoporum orthodo-xorum & aliorum Christianorum vitia negant esse Ecclesiam, Audiani, Donatistae.
units.tr: Because of the faults of orthodox bishops and other Christians, they deny that the church is the Church: the Audians, Donatists.

units.la: Sanctam.
units.tr: Holy.

units.la: Vitae turpitudinem probant Severiani, Origeniani, Aetiani, Eunomiani.
units.tr: They defend a life of baseness: the Severians, Origenians, Aetians, Eunomians.

units.la: Ecclesiam perfecte sanctam hic debere esse contendunt Novatiani, Donatistae.
units.tr: They contend that the Church here ought to be perfectly holy: the Novatians, Donatists.

units.la: Communionem Sanctorum.
units.tr: The communion of saints.

units.la: Bona omnia inter Christianos esse debere communia, etiam quoad dominij ius, dicunt Anabaptistae, Jesuitae.
units.tr: They say that all goods ought to be held in common among Christians, even as regards the right of ownership: the Anabaptists, Jesuits.

units.la: Uxores inter Christianos communes esse debere, Nicolaitae.
units.tr: That wives ought to be held in common among Christians: the Nicolaitans.

units.la: Remissionem peccatorum. De peccato.
units.tr: Forgiveness of sins. On sin.

units.la: Peccatū a natura non a culpa hominibus ines-se dicunt Saturniniani, Manichaei.
units.tr: The Saturnians and Manichaeans say that sin is inherent in humans by nature, not by fault.

units.la: Peccata a fato & stellarum constellatione esse dicunt Priscillianistae.
units.tr: The Priscillianists say that sins come from fate and the constellation of the stars.

units.la: Peccatum esse substantiam dicunt Manichaei.
units.tr: The Manichaeans say that sin is a substance.

units.la: Peccata omnia esse aequalia, Iovinianistae.
units.tr: The Jovinianists say that all sins are equal.

units.la: Peccatum originale nullum esse, Pelagiani, Celestiani.
units.tr: The Pelagians and Caelestians say that there is no original sin.

units.la: De remissione.
units.tr: On remission.

units.la: Peccata non omnia, sed inuoluntaria tātum, remitti dicunt Basilidiani.
units.tr: The Basilideans say that not all sins are forgiven, but only involuntary ones.

units.la: Peccata per unctionem, & certas caeremo-nias, non per solum Christi sanguinem remitti dicunt Heracleonita, Helcesaita.
units.tr: The Heracleonites and Helcesaites say that sins are forgiven through anointing and certain ceremonies, not through the blood of Christ alone.

units.la: Peccatorum remissionem operibus & ora-tioni tribuunt Messaliani, Euchetae.
units.tr: The Messalians and Euchites ascribe the forgiveness of sins to works and prayer.

units.la: Peccatorum remissionem denegant lapsis, Cathari.
units.tr: The Cathari deny forgiveness of sins to the lapsed.

units.la: Lapsis post baptismum, Nouatiani, Quartadecimani, & Apostolici, & Meletiani.
units.tr: The Novatians, Quartodecimans, Apostolics and Meletians deny it to those who lapse after baptism.

units.la: Clericis & Episcopis tantum post gradum assumptum lapsis, Luciferiani.
units.tr: The Luciferians deny it only to clergy and bishops who lapse after they have taken up their office.

units.la: Carnis resurrectionem.
units.tr: The resurrection of the body.

units.la: Carnis resurrectionem negant Simoniani, Sa-turniniani, Basilidiani, Carpocratiani, Valentinia-ni, & Marcita, Ophita, Caiani, Sethiani, Archontici, Cerdoniani, & Marcionita, Apellita, Seueriani, Bar-desanista, Heraclita, Seleuciani, Hermiani, Pro-cliani.
units.tr: The Simonians, Saturnians, Basilideans, Carpocratians, Valentinians, Marcitae, Ophites, Caianites, Sethians, Archonticks, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Apellites, Severians, Bardesanists, Heraclites, Seleucians, Hermians and Proclians deny the resurrection of the body.

units.la: Carnis resurrectionem iam factam esse di-cunt, Hymenaeus, Philetus, Menandriani.
units.tr: Hymenaeus, Philetus and the Menandrians say that the resurrection of the body has already taken place.

units.la: Animas quoque resurrecturas dicunt A-rabiti[?].
units.tr: They also say that souls will rise again: the Arabites[?].

units.la: Animas hominum non dissolui quidem mor-te, sed in sepulchris dormire usque ad diem re-surrectionis, Psychopannychitae.
units.tr: The Psychopannychites say that human souls are not indeed dissolved by death, but sleep in the tombs until the day of resurrection.

units.la: Pro resurrectione inducunt μετεμψύχωσιν, si-ue reuolutionem animarum, Basilidiani, Carpo-cratiani, Marcionitae, Origenistae, & Manichaei.
units.tr: In place of resurrection they introduce metempsychosis [μετεμψύχωσις], or the transmigration of souls: the Basilideans, Carpocratians, Marcionites, Origenists and Manichaeans.

units.la: Animas hominum sceleratorum transire in daemonas, Tertullianista.
units.tr: The Tertullianists say that the souls of wicked men pass into demons.

units.la: Vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Eternal life.

units.la: Vitam aeternam esse extra Dei regnum & paradisum dicunt Pelagiani, Celestiani.
units.tr: The Pelagians and Caelestians say that eternal life lies outside the kingdom of God and paradise.

units.la: Vitam aeternam post resurrectionem constituunt in corporis voluptate & in hac terra, quae duratura sit mille tantum annos, Cerinthiani, Nepotiani, Chiliastae, Aeternales.
units.tr: The Cerinthians, Nepotians, Chiliasts and Aeternales place eternal life after the resurrection in bodily pleasure and on this earth, which is to last only a thousand years.

units.la: Vitam aeternam & Ierusalem caelestem esse in hac terra dicunt Pepuziani.
units.tr: The Pepuzians say that eternal life and the heavenly Jerusalem are on this earth.

units.la: De gloria beatorum nugantur, Montanistae.
units.tr: The Montanists trifle about the glory of the blessed.

units.la: Paradisum verum esse coetus Ecclesiae, qui sunt in his terris, Adamitae.
units.tr: The Adamites say that the true paradise is the assembly of the Church that is on these lands.

units.la: Paradisum terrenum fuisse certum locum negant, Origenistae, Hierachitae.
units.tr: The Origenists and Hierachites deny that earthly paradise was a definite place.

units.la: Paruulos ad regnum Dei pertinere negant Hierachitae.
units.tr: The Hierachites deny that little children belong to the kingdom of God.

units.la: De inferno.
units.tr: On hell.

units.la: Poenas peccatorum esse in hac tantum vita dicunt Basilidiani.
units.tr: The Basilideans say that the punishments of sinners exist in this life only.

units.la: Poenas aeternas esse temporaneas, & diabolos esse saluandos, Origenistae, Liberatores.
units.tr: The Origenists and Liberators say that eternal punishments are temporary, and that the devils are to be saved.

units.la: Limbos & purgatorium pro inferno substituunt Papistae.
units.tr: The Papists substitute limbo and purgatory for hell.

units.la: DE ORATIONE.
units.tr: ON PRAYER.

units.la: Orandum Deum negat Prodiciani, Adamitae.
units.tr: The Prodiciani and the Adamites deny that God is to be prayed to.

units.la: Orationi vim & causam salutis nostrae tribuunt, Messaliani, Euchetae, Monachi.
units.tr: The Messalians, the Euchites and the monks attribute to prayer the power and cause of our salvation.

units.la: DE SACRAMENTIS.
units.tr: On the Sacraments.

units.la: Sacramenta omnino tollunt Archontici, Afcodruta.
units.tr: The Archontici and Ascodrutae abolish the sacraments altogether.

units.la: Ulum sacramentorum spernunt Messaliani, Anabaptista.
units.tr: The Messaliani and Anabaptista despise the use of the sacraments.

units.la: Sacramentorum effectum ministrorum sanctitati & manui attribuunt Donatista.
units.tr: The Donatista attribute the effect of the sacraments to the holiness and hands of the ministers.

units.la: Operi operato, Papista.
units.tr: By the work done (opus operatum): Papista.

units.la: Sacramenta per mulieres dari posse dicunt Marcionita, Pepuziani, Papista.
units.tr: The Marcionita, Pepuziani and Papista say that the sacraments can be given by women.

units.la: Sacramenta plura, quàm Christus ipse, instituunt Papista.
units.tr: The Papista institute more sacraments than Christ himself did.

units.la: De Baptismo.
units.tr: On Baptism.

units.la: Baptismum aliquem visibilem esse dandum Christianis negant Afcodruta.
units.tr: The Afcodruta deny that any visible baptism should be given to Christians.

units.la: Baptismum Christi nec bonum, nec utilem esse, sed suum tantùm dicunt Samofatenian, Manichaei, Arriani, Aetiani.
units.tr: The Samofatenian, Manichaei, Arriani and Aetiani say that Christ's baptism is neither good nor useful, but only their own.

units.la: Baptismum Christi spernunt Pelagiani, Celestiani, Catabaptista.
units.tr: The Pelagiani, Celestiani and Catabaptista despise Christ's baptism.

units.la: Baptismum Christi conspurcant Marcita, Papista.
units.tr: The Marcita and Papista defile Christ's baptism.

units.la: Baptismum in aqua faciedum negant Marcionita, Seleuciani, Hermiani, Procliani.
units.tr: The Marcionita, Seleuciani, Hermiani and Procliani deny that baptism is to be performed in water.

units.la: Baptismi vim ad præterita tantùm peccata delenda pertinere, Messaliani, Papista.
units.tr: The Messaliani and Papista hold that the power of baptism extends only to the deleting of past sins.

units.la: Baptismum paruulis fidelium negant dandum Pelagiani.
units.tr: The Pelagiani deny that the baptism of the infants of believers is to be given.

units.la: Coniugibus Christianis denegant Marcionita.
units.tr: The Marcionita deny it to Christian spouses.

units.la: Post Baptismum homines peccare non posse, Iouinianista.
units.tr: The Iouinianista hold that after baptism men cannot sin.

units.la: Inferiores hominis partes negant baptizandas Eunomiani.
units.tr: The Eunomiani deny that the lower parts of the man are to be baptized.

units.la: Baptizatos ab orthodoxis, rebaptizandos dicunt Nouatiani, Arriani, Aetiani, Donatistæ.
units.tr: The Nouatiani, Arriani, Aetiani and Donatistæ say that those baptized by the orthodox must be rebaptized.

units.la: Baptisma etiam in suis à se baptizatis sæpius repetunt Marcionitæ, Nouatiani, Cathari, Ana-baptistæ.
units.tr: The Marcionitæ, Nouatiani, Cathari and Anabaptistæ repeat baptism again and again, even in those they have themselves baptized.

units.la: Pro mortuis catechumenis alios substituunt baptizandos, Marcionitæ.
units.tr: The Marcionitæ substitute others to be baptized in place of catechumens who have died.

units.la: Homines iam mortuos baptizat Montanistæ.
units.tr: The Montanistæ baptize men who are already dead.

units.la: De Eucharistia siue Cœna Domini.
units.tr: On the Eucharist or the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Cœnam Domini spernunt Messaliani.
units.tr: The Messaliani despise the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Cœnam Domini conspurcant Marcitæ, O-phitæ.
units.tr: The Marcitæ and Ophitæ defile the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Cœnam Domini, vt Pascha antiquum, diei decimæquartæ mensis astringunt Quartideci-mani, Floriani.
units.tr: The Quartodecimani and Floriani bind the Lord's Supper, like the ancient Passover, to the fourteenth day of the month.

units.la: In Cœna Domini signa necessaria negant A-scodrutæ.
units.tr: The Ascodrutæ deny that signs are necessary in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Signa tollunt, & transsubstantiant in re ipsam signatam Papistæ.
units.tr: The Papistæ remove the signs and transubstantiate them into the very thing signified.

units.la: Vinum damnant, & eius usum in Cœna Domini Seueriani.
units.tr: The Seueriani condemn wine and its use in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Aquam pro vino. in Eucharistia substituunt Tatiani, Encratitæ, Aquarii[?].
units.tr: The Tatiani, Encratitæ and Aquarii[?] substitute water for wine in the Eucharist.

units.la: Pane Cœnæ Domini sanguini humano per-miscent Cataphryges, Pepuziani:
units.tr: The Cataphryges and Pepuziani mix human blood with the bread of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Semini humano, Gnostici, Manichæi.
units.tr: The Gnostici and Manichæi mix human semen with it.

units.la: Panem non esse carnis, sed diuinitatis Christi signum, dicunt Armenii.
units.tr: The Armenii say that the bread is not a sign of Christ's flesh but of his divinity.

units.la: Azymo pane præcisè & necessariò in Cœna Domini utendum esse dicunt Armenii.
units.tr: The Armenii say that unleavened bread must be used precisely and necessarily in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Similam & farinam summis tantùm digitis apprehensam, pro pane in Cœna Domini accipiunt Basaniani[?], Similitæ.
units.tr: The Basaniani[?] and Similitæ take semolina and flour, handled only with the tips of the fingers, in place of bread in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Præter duo signa à Christo instituta, alia addunt, nempe aquam, Aquarij, Papistæ:caseum, Artotyritæ.
units.tr: Beyond the two signs instituted by Christ, they add others: water, as do the Aquarij and Papistæ; cheese, as do the Artotyritæ.

units.la: Sine pœnitentia quoslibet peccatores, etiam sceleratissimos homines, ad Cœnam Domini admittunt Audiani.
units.tr: The Audiani admit to the Lord's Supper, without repentance, any sinners whatever, even the most wicked men.

units.la: INDEX QUARTUS, qui est rerum & verborum quae in hoc opere continentur.
units.tr: FOURTH INDEX, of the things and words contained in this work.
